title: British Empire
capsule: In this mid-period, the British Empire's center of gravity shifted decisively to Asia after the East India Company's 1757 victory at Plassey delivered control of Bengal, transforming a chartered trading company into a territorial ruler backed by sepoy armies. Successive Anglo-Mysore and Anglo-Maratha wars extended Company rule across most of the Indian subcontinent by 1818, while Company and Crown forces also secured Cape Colony, Ceylon, and Singapore as strategic way-stations on Indian Ocean trade routes. This corporate-military phase of expansion ended in 1858, when the Government of India Act transferred rule from the East India Company directly to the British Crown in the wake of the 1857 Indian Rebellion, with the last Company forces stood down by 1859.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial boundaries of British colonial possessions in this period are well documented through Admiralty charts, Colonial Office records, and treaty texts; internal frontier zones in West Africa and parts of Central Asia are approximate, but core territories are precisely attested.
